# lambda-trigger-sqs

Creates an SQS event source mapping that invokes a Lambda function when messages arrive in a queue. Supports batch configuration, event filtering, and partial batch failure reporting. Works with both standard and FIFO queues.

## Usage

```hcl
module "sqs_trigger" {
  source = "../../modules/lambda-trigger-sqs"

  function_name = module.my_function.function_name
  function_arn  = module.my_function.function_arn
  role_name     = module.my_function.role_name
  queue_arn     = aws_sqs_queue.tasks.arn

  batch_size                     = 5
  report_batch_item_failures     = true
}
```

## IAM Model

This is a **pull-based** trigger. Lambda polls the SQS queue, so the execution role needs permission to read from it. The module attaches a policy granting `sqs:ReceiveMessage`, `sqs:DeleteMessage`, and `sqs:GetQueueAttributes` on the queue ARN to the provided `role_name`.

This means `role_name` is required. Use the core module's `role_name` output (which is non-null when the module creates the role).

## Queue Management

The module does not create or manage the SQS queue itself (BYO queue). Dead-letter queue (DLQ) configuration, redrive policies, and queue settings are the user's responsibility on the `aws_sqs_queue` resource.

FIFO queues are supported automatically — no special configuration is needed in this module. AWS handles in-order delivery and exactly-once processing based on the queue type.

## Inputs

### Required

| Name | Type | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `function_name` | `string` | Name of the Lambda function. Used for IAM policy naming. |
| `function_arn` | `string` | ARN of the Lambda function. Used by the event source mapping. |
| `role_name` | `string` | Name of the Lambda execution role. The module attaches an SQS read policy to this role. Must not be `null` — use the core module's `role_name` output. |
| `queue_arn` | `string` | ARN of the SQS queue to poll. Works with both standard and FIFO queues. |

### Optional

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `batch_size` | `number` | `10` | Maximum number of messages per batch sent to the Lambda function. Range: `1` to `10000` (standard queues) or `1` to `10` (FIFO queues). |
| `maximum_batching_window_in_seconds` | `number` | `0` | Maximum time in seconds to gather messages before invoking the function. Range: `0` to `300`. Set to `0` (default) for immediate invocation. Values above `0` reduce invocations at the cost of latency. |
| `report_batch_item_failures` | `bool` | `false` | Enable partial batch failure reporting. When `true`, the Lambda function can return a list of failed message IDs, and only those messages are retried. When `false`, a single failure causes the entire batch to be retried. The function must return a `batchItemFailures` response — see [AWS documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/with-sqs.html#services-sqs-batchfailurereporting). |
| `filter_criteria` | `list(object)` | `[]` | Event filtering criteria. Each object has a `pattern` field containing a JSON-encoded filter pattern. Only messages matching at least one pattern are delivered to the function. See [AWS documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/invocation-eventfiltering.html) for pattern syntax. |
| `tags` | `map(string)` | `{}` | Map of tags applied to all resources (IAM policy). |

**`filter_criteria` object fields:**

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `pattern` | `string` | JSON-encoded filter pattern. Example: `jsonencode({"body": {"type": ["order"]}})` to only process order messages. |

## Outputs

| Name | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `event_source_mapping_id` | ID of the Lambda event source mapping. |
